blocks.text: Imagine building a bridge without knowing where it should lead or who will use it. Eliciting requirements in software engineering is about defining what to build before starting the construction.

blocks.markdown: In software engineering, eliciting requirements is a critical phase where the needs and expectations of stakeholders are gathered and documented. This process helps in understanding what the software should do and the constraints it must operate under.

blocks.title: Stakeholder
blocks.text: A stakeholder is any person or group who has an interest in the success or failure of a project. This includes users, customers, developers, and managers.

blocks.markdown: The first step in requirements elicitation is identifying stakeholders. Stakeholders provide the necessary insights into what the software should achieve. The next step is gathering information through various techniques such as interviews, surveys, and workshops.

blocks.title: User Story
blocks.text: A user story is a simple description of a software feature from the perspective of an end user. It typically follows the format: 'As a [type of user], I want [an action] so that [a benefit].'

blocks.markdown: User stories are a popular way to express requirements in agile development. They are short, simple, and focus on the user's needs. Each user story should have acceptance criteria that define the conditions under which the story is considered complete.

blocks.title: Writing a User Story
blocks.prompt: Write a user story for a library management system feature that allows users to reserve books online.

steps.text: Identify the type of user involved.
Determine the action the user wants to perform.
Define the benefit the user receives from this action.
Combine these elements into the user story format.

blocks.answer: As a library member, I want to reserve books online so that I can ensure availability when I visit the library.

blocks.title: Functional vs. Non-Functional Requirements
blocks.text: Functional requirements specify what the system should do, while non-functional requirements define how the system performs a function.

rows: The system shall allow users to log in.
Describes system attributes such as performance, usability, reliability.
The system shall respond to user actions within 2 seconds.
blocks.caption: Comparison of Functional and Non-Functional Requirements

blocks.title: Identifying Stakeholders
blocks.prompt: A new e-commerce platform is being developed. Identify three potential stakeholders and explain their interest in the project.

steps.text: Consider who will use the platform.
Think about who will maintain the platform.
Identify who will benefit financially from the platform.

blocks.answer: 1. Customers: They will use the platform to purchase products and are interested in a user-friendly experience. 2. Developers: They will maintain the platform and are interested in a clear set of requirements. 3. Business Owners: They will benefit financially and are interested in the platform's ability to attract and retain customers.

blocks.markdown: Eliciting requirements is not just about gathering information but also about ensuring that the requirements are complete and feasible. This involves validating the requirements with stakeholders and refining them as needed.

points: Eliciting requirements involves identifying stakeholders and gathering their needs.
User stories and acceptance criteria are essential for capturing and validating requirements.
Distinguishing between functional and non-functional requirements is crucial for a comprehensive requirement set.
